headline: Highest risk is medium: shared-document workflows can create prompt-injection and cascading-error paths, while direct leakage/conflict are limited by marker’s no-write/no-network profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: marker is a document-processing agent with read/write/network disabled, so it can still ingest untrusted document content; nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress and could consume marker outputs in a workflow. No shared channel is documented, so the interaction is inferred and uncertainty pushes severity up from low.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill receives marker-generated document text as task input without provenance checks, injection is plausible.
IF an operator manually copies marker output into nuwa-skill prompts, attacker-controlled instructions can traverse the pair.
mitigations: Add a provenance banner to all marker outputs.
Strip instructions from extracted text before passing to nuwa-skill.
Require human review of any document-derived prompt.
Use a fixed template that separates data from instructions.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance tagging between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: marker cannot read or write the filesystem and has no network egress, so it is unlikely to leak data directly. nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress, but no sensitive data classes or shared workspace are documented, so the pairwise leakage path is limited and not default-dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents are placed in a shared workspace with sensitive files, leakage risk increases.
IF nuwa-skill is given confidential text from marker, it may transmit that text to allowlisted endpoints.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not pass confidential documents into nuwa-skill.
Review allowlisted destinations before use.
Redact secrets from marker outputs before handoff.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries and egress policy checks.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: marker has no filesystem write, no subprocesses, no shell, and no git modification, so it cannot contend for mutable local resources with nuwa-skill. nuwa-skill exposes only allowlisted network egress in the profile, so no overlapping write surface is documented.
conditions: IF future deployment grants both agents write access to the same directory, conflict risk would change.
IF nuwa-skill is extended with local write or git permissions, reassess for contention.
mitigations: Keep marker read-only.
Avoid granting nuwa-skill local write permissions.
Run both agents under separate service accounts.
Document any shared mutable resource before deployment.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared writes are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: marker can produce extracted document text that nuwa-skill may treat as input, and no verification or provenance controls are documented. Because nuwa-skill is not documented as taking action beyond research workflows, the blast radius is moderate rather than high, but the inference is uncertain so medium is safer.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill consumes marker output as authoritative without cross-checking, errors can cascade.
IF marker extraction is used to populate downstream research artifacts, a single hallucinated field can propagate.
mitigations: Require source-document cross-checks before downstream use.
Mark marker output as untrusted until verified.
Add a review step before nuwa-skill acts on extracted facts.
Log provenance for each derived claim.
requires-engineering: implement citation-backed validation between extraction and research steps.

E_compliance.rationale: No regulated data classes, residency constraints, retention policies, or certifications are documented for either agent, so there is no evidenced compliance mismatch. The pairwise compliance pathway is therefore not established from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned PHI, EU PII, or other regulated data, compliance must be reassessed.
IF deployment policies impose residency or retention constraints, verify both agents against them.
mitigations: Record the data classes each agent may touch.
Check residency and retention requirements before deployment.
Avoid routing regulated data through undocumented workflows.
Add a compliance review gate for new data classes.
requires-engineering: attach policy metadata to each agent.
